# Building Stronger Corporate-Charity Partnerships


16 Nov 2026


[Global](https://www.diageo.com/en/news-and-media/stories?region=global)[Positive Drinking](https://www.diageo.com/en/news-and-media/stories?topic=positive-drinking)[ESG](https://www.diageo.com/en/news-and-media/stories?topic=esg)[2026](https://www.diageo.com/en/news-and-media/stories?year=2026)

“We must continue to build stronger corporate-charity partnerships formed around a material risk like harmful drinking. Men’s Sheds is the perfect example of this.” Elisabeth Rochford, ESG Lead, Diageo


As a responsible business, we want to change the way people drink, for the better. This is why we promote responsible drinking and invest in education programmes to encourage positive drinking behaviours.


Diageo’s commitment to promoting positive drinking is a core pillar of our Spirit of Progress action plan. How we activate this work takes different forms and depends on the audience.


Older men, for example, are not the easiest cohort to influence, but an important one. Public health data suggests that older men in Britain are more likely to drink more frequently than any other age group, and are more likely to consume alcohol to levels described as ‘increasing risk’. These trends are often influenced by life-stage or age-related factors, such as retirement or loss of purpose, bereavement, divorce, and diminishing family and social connections.


That’s why three years ago, Diageo and the UK Men’s Sheds Association (UKMSA) came together to address this reality for thousands of older men through our DRINKiQ programme. DRINKiQ is Diageo’s alcohol education platform, seeking to educate and enable consumers to try to make informed choices. Incredible organisations like the UKMSA show that creative and social community spaces can change lives for the better. Sheds improve wellbeing indicators, including the moderation of alcohol consumption of older men, as they navigate age-related life changes.


Indeed, for many of these men, alcohol consumption does not increase in later life in a vacuum. It does so because of a vacuum, where life changes can mean more time on your hands and more time on your own. The shift is usually subtle. It could look like more frequent evenings in front of the TV, countless hours playing bridge online, or spending more time at the pub, where one or two pints a couple of nights a week quietly becomes three or four, several nights a week.


And the reversal of that is what Sheds demonstrates – that meaningful social outlets can improve physical and mental health outcomes like alleviating stress, easing loneliness and encouraging healthier habits around alcohol. “I’ve visited many Sheds and met countless Shedders ready with a story, a joke or a warm welcome. I always leave with a smile on my face.”


We have recently renewed the partnership for another three years, helping UKMSA to scale its presence and support even more Sheds. Campaigning is an integral part of our work together, so that we help spread the word about the vital role Sheds play in the lives of older men and their communities.


Last year, we launched a joint campaign to bring the magic of Sheds outside: “Mission: Shoulder to Shoulder”.


###### Pictured: Shedders from Winterslow Men’s Shed in Wiltshire seated on their bench outside of the town hall.


Over the past year, Shedders across the UK have taken on the “Mission” to create and install unique buddy benches in their communities, to help facilitate the chance conversations that can brighten a day – or even change a life. We ran a unique social experiment which observed public benches across the country, and found that a bench would, on average, facilitate 5.5 conversations daily and 2,002 yearly. With 100 benches installed nationally, Shedders are facilitating over 200,000 conversations annually.


###### Pictured: Diageo volunteers alongside Shedders at St Martin’s Shed in South London.


TV icon Timmy Mallett joined Black Park Shed in Slough to help Shedders Arun Lloyd and Mark Lemon build bench number one. From there the “Mission” quickly gathered momentum. Diageo volunteers got involved too, picking up tools at St Martin’s Shed in London. Hundreds more Shedders built and installed benches in their communities. This bench in Salisbury, aptly named Drawing People Together, stands outside the town hall as an invitation to stop, sit and start a conversation that could make all the difference.


###### Pictured: TV icon Timmy Mallett alongside Shedders at Black Park Shed in Slough.


I look forward to what else we can deliver with our partners like UKMSA and alongside other organisations, in the years to come.


**About Diageo** ****


Diageo is a global leader in beverage alcohol with an outstanding collection of brands across spirits and beer categories. These brands include Johnnie Walker, Crown Royal, JεB and Buchanan's whiskies, Smirnoff and Ketel One vodkas, Captain Morgan, Baileys, Don Julio, Tanqueray and Guinness.


Diageo is a global company, and our products are sold in nearly 180 countries around the world. The company is listed on both the London Stock Exchange (DGE) and the New York Stock Exchange (DEO). For more information about Diageo, our people, our brands, and performance, visit us at[www.diageo.com](https://www.diageo.com/) .
